item.title: DataNexus Architecture: Four Layers and Two Flows
item.description: Why ontology-based routing instead of a single NL2SQL pipeline — and what the second flow, from Pull to Push, looks like

item.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: On-Device Multimodal Search in One Vector Space
item.description: Google’s EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, code, images, video, and audio into a shared 768-dimensional space with optional encoders for on-device search.

item.title: Document Layout Analysis and Parsing for Enterprise RAG Accuracy
item.description: Preserving tables, coordinates, and visual structure during PDF parsing improves embedding quality and cuts hallucinations in enterprise RAG pipelines.

item.title: OpenKB: Turning Scattered Documents into a Connected Local AI Wiki
item.description: OpenKB compiles local documents into an interlinked AI wiki using PageIndex tree indexing without a vector database.

item.title: A 6-Stage Selection Framework for Keeping RAG Architectures Simple
item.description: Start RAG systems with BM25 keyword search plus LLM query rewriting before adding Vector DBs and rerankers, scaling across 6 stages based on 5 data criteria.

item.title: Local Korean PII Detection and Pseudonymization with ko-pii
item.description: ko-pii detects and pseudonymizes 33 Korean personal data types locally using Python’s standard library, regex rules, and checksums with zero external API calls.

item.title: Microsoft Ontology Playground: Free Browser Tool for Learning Ontologies
item.description: Explore Microsoft’s free Ontology Playground for designing interactive entity-relationship graphs, importing/exporting RDF files, and prototyping GraphRAG schemas.

item.title: MaxKB: An Open-Source Agent Platform Unifying RAG and Workflows

item.description: Chunked vector RAG loses cross-document links and version freshness. Restructuring internal docs into a linked LLM Wiki improves multi-hop accuracy and cuts cost.

item.title: Three Core Skills and Portfolio Strategies for Aspiring AI PMs
item.description: Moving from deterministic software to probabilistic AI products requires AI literacy, distribution-aware metrics, failure design, and documented build logs.

item.title: MemPalace: A Local Open-Source Hierarchical Memory System for AI

item.title: Optimizing Korean Search on Databricks AI Search with Kiwi
item.description: Databricks AI Search lacks built-in Nori support. Adding pre-index morphological tokenization and synonym expansion with Kiwi boosts Korean BM25 recall.

item.title: Jikji: Deterministic File Maps and Local Search for AI Agents
item.description: Open-source Jikji replaces heavy vector databases and wasteful CLI grep loops with cached file maps, LLM Wiki pages, and deterministic graph routing.

item.title: Enhans AMD: Query Expansion Through Socratic Multi-Agent Dialogue
item.description: AMD expands ambiguous search queries and improves retrieval accuracy through Socratic questioning and multi-agent verification.

item.title: Google Research's Agentic RAG and the Sufficient Context Agent
item.description: Google Research’s Agentic RAG uses a Sufficient Context Agent to verify retrieved evidence iteratively, reaching 90.1% cross-corpus accuracy on FramesQA.

item.title: Adaptive Chunking: Selecting the Right RAG Strategy per Document
item.description: Adaptive Chunking scores candidate splits with five label-free intrinsic metrics to pick the best chunking strategy for each document in a RAG pipeline.

item.title: Real-Time GraphRAG Without Prebuilt Knowledge Graphs: LogicRAG
item.description: LogicRAG skips expensive offline graph construction by building query-time reasoning DAGs with topological sorting and rolling memory.

item.title: RAG-Anything: Multimodal RAG Across Text, Images, Tables, and Equations
item.description: HKUDS’s LightRAG-based framework links text, images, tables, and formulas in a dual graph, posting gains on DocBench and MMLongBench.

item.title: How Decades of Document Parsing Tech Topped GitHub Trending
item.description: A Korean software company hit #1 on GitHub Trending by open-sourcing its PDF extraction engine instead of selling a monolithic office suite.

item.title: Smart Chunking Strategies That Raise RAG Retrieval Accuracy
item.description: Why fixed-length text splitting breaks RAG context, and how heading metadata, Markdown conversion, and layout-aware dynamic overlap fix retrieval.

item.title: 5. Automating Metadata Maintenance: Karpathy's LLM Wiki Architecture
item.description: RAG starts from scratch every time. Karpathy proposes having the LLM maintain a wiki directly so knowledge accumulates. DataNexus’s ontology catalog needs the same principle to avoid abandonment.

item.title: OpenDocuments: Local RAG Across Scattered Team Knowledge
item.description: An open-source on-premise RAG platform that connects docs across Notion, GitHub, and S3 to local LLMs without external API calls.

item.title: Beopmang: Pre-Parsed Korean Statute JSON and Vector Search for AI Agents
item.description: Parsing raw government statute XML breaks tables and burns preprocessing time. Beopmang serves Korean statutes as clean JSON with built-in pgvector search.

item.title: Self-Hosting Team RAG with OpenDocuments, SQLite, and LanceDB
item.description: OpenDocuments unifies scattered docs from Notion, GitHub, and S3 into a local Ollama-backed RAG stack built on TypeScript, SQLite, and LanceDB.

item.title: Unexpected Limits When Extracting Web Pages to Markdown with defuddle
item.description: Testing defuddle for RAG web ingestion shows sharp quality swings: non-semantic HTML mixes ads into body text, while client-rendered pages drop content.

item.title: Practical Agent Design Lessons from the OpenAI Guide
item.description: Handing open-ended planning to an LLM causes production loops and stalls. OpenAI’s practical guide solves this with explicit state-machine workflow control.

item.title: Why Preprocessing Drives RAG Quality: Converting Docs with MarkItDown
item.description: MarkItDown converts PDFs and Office files into Markdown while preserving tables and heading hierarchies, cutting RAG preprocessing work.

item.title: 1. Why We're Building DataNexus
item.description: The structural problems with enterprise data analytics, and why we decided to build an ontology-based data agent platform.
